segments.summary: Capability metadata, catalog snapshots, role mapping, compaction thresholds, transforms, and runtime request routing were reviewed; the strongest gaps concern refresh atomicity, threshold invariants, transform idempotence, and deterministic API-family routing.

Availability lifecycle, pricing, billing attribution, token counting, and context usage views were reviewed; lifecycle races, pricing version semantics, billing alias migration, token-adapter recovery, and partial-data GUI behavior remain underspecified.

Bedrock compatibility and web-provider routing were reviewed; explicit mapping and taxonomy boundaries are strong, while mirrored-registry drift, best-effort completeness, and Firecrawl credential or URL validation need executable contracts.

Tavily policy, web-operation mirrors, automation sessions, Persona preferences, skipped controls, and variant ownership were reviewed; automation authority lifecycle and delegated validation seams are critical negative-space findings.

Variant definition, resolution, configuration, disabling, cycling, persistence, and Persona schema were reviewed; deterministic ranking, invalid-config disposition, active-disable transitions, and concurrent session mutation are not fully specified.

Persona preselection, aliases, media aliases, canonical GUI identity, picker display, and requested overrides were reviewed; alias collisions, target validation, accessibility, localization, and selected-surface loss are principal gaps.

Settings availability, refresh, runtime effort, legacy migration, and inspectors were reviewed; GUI truth boundaries are strong, while overlapping refresh sequencing and partial-failure recovery remain high-risk gaps.

OpenCode baselines, Puppet Master deltas, and acceptance criteria were reviewed; deterministic identity and Persona fallback have clear oracles, while invalid custom-variant terminal disposition remains ambiguous.
